## "Look, you got my shoes all bloody. Lick them. I said lick my shoes clean, scum!"

##### Source: adapted from [Benjamin Huffman's Pugilist v3](https://www.dmsguild.com/product/184921/The-Pugilist-Class)

### Bonus Proficiency

When you choose this discipline at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Intimidation skill if you don’t have it already. If you do, you gain proficiency in your choice of the Deception or Sleight of Hand skill.

### Boisterous Taunt

Also at 3rd level, you become a master at pissing people off. You can use a bonus action on your turn to provoke a creature within 60 feet who can see or hear you. That creature must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the creature takes software damage equal to a roll of your hands die + your Charisma modifier and has disadvantage on any attack rolls it makes that do not include you as a target before the start of your next turn.

For this, any of your other Dirty Dog features that require your opponent to make a saving throw, the saving DC is calculated as follows:

**Dirty Dog save DC** = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier

### Dirty Deeds

Starting at 6th level, you know a few things that help you even the odds when the going gets rough. You can use each of these tricks once and regain their use when you finish a short or long rest.

- **Stomp.** When you deal damage with an unarmed strike, you attempt to slow the creature you hit. The creature must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, you regain 1 expended mettle point and the creature’s movement speed is halved for one minute.
- **Sweep the Leg.** When you deal damage with an unarmed strike, you can choose to knock a creature off its feet by sweeping their legs out. The creature must make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, you regain 1 expended mettle point and the creature is knocked prone.
- **Sand Kick.** You can use a bonus action to attempt to blind a creature within 5 feet. The creature must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, you regain 1 expended mettle point and the creature is blinded until the end of its next turn.

### Grating Words

Starting at 11th level, your threats and dirty deeds pack an extra punch. When you make a Charisma (Intimidation) check, you can use your reaction and spend 1 mettle to give yourself advantage on the roll. When a creature makes a saving throw against one of your Dirty Dog features, you can use your reaction and spend 1 mettle to give that roll disadvantage.

### Loudmouthed

Starting at 17th level, you gain the ability to piss every creature in the room off with minimal effort. When you use your Boisterous Taunt feature, you can choose to target a number of creatures within 60 feet who can see or hear you up to your level in this class, instead of a single creature. You regain 1 expended mettle point the first time each of these targets hits you with an attack before the start of your next turn. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.
